explanations.prose-discipline.frozen-verb:
prose-discipline.frozen-verb -- Put the action in the verb
kind: pattern   severity: error   scope: prose
tiers: strict=enforced  normal=enforced  relaxed=advisory

"<match>" freezes the action in a noun. Use the plain verb.

Fix: Promote the noun to a finite verb and delete the general-purpose verb and its article.

Named exceptions (a suppression must cite one):
  - identifier-fidelity
  - quotation
  - code-span
  - legal-force
  - api-name

  <!-- slopvac-allow: rule=prose-discipline.frozen-verb reason=identifier-fidelity -->

Examples
  - The runner performs an analysis of the coverage report.
  + The runner analyzes the coverage report.
  - Conduct an investigation of the failing shard.
  + Investigate the failing shard.
  - The hook provides validation of the payload.
  + The hook validates the payload.

Source: ASD-STE100
  ASD-STE100 rule 3.7 (Issue 9)
  Both sources name this. Orwell's operators-or-verbal-false-limbs paragraph calls the pattern "the elimination of simple verbs"; the specification requires a verb for an action. Overlaps orwell-voice.passive-voice on sentences that are both passive and frozen, which is correct: they carry two defects and the fix differs.
explanations.prose-discipline.run-on:
prose-discipline.run-on -- Split the run-on
kind: metric   severity: warning   scope: sentence
tiers: strict=enforced  normal=enforced  relaxed=advisory

This sentence stitches <match> independent ideas together; the limit is <replacement>. Split it.

Fix: Split at the clause boundary that carries the least shared context.

Named exceptions (a suppression must cite one):
  - quotation
  - code-span
  - vertical-list
  - legal-force

  <!-- slopvac-allow: rule=prose-discipline.run-on reason=quotation -->

Examples
  - The parser reads the file, and it normalizes the paths; then it emits the report, but it skips any entry that fails validation, which the caller must handle separately.
  + The parser reads the file and normalizes the paths. It emits the report and skips any entry that fails validation. The caller handles those separately.

Source: ASD-STE100
  ASD-STE100 rule 4.1 (Issue 9)
  Counts coordinating conjunctions, semicolons, dashes used as clause joins, and non-restrictive "which" clauses, rather than words. A sentence under the word cap can still carry four ideas, and that is the defect a reader feels. Threshold 3 permits a compound sentence with a trailing qualifier and rejects the fourth stitch.

kind: metric   severity: error   scope: sentence
tiers: strict=enforced  normal=enforced  relaxed=enforced

This sentence has <value> words. Use twenty-five or fewer.

Fix: Split the sentence at a clause boundary.

Named exceptions (a suppression must cite one):

  - code-span

Examples

Source: ASD-STE100
  ASD-STE100 rule 6.3 (Issue 9)
  Same word-counting contract as the procedural cap, five words wider. A note inside a procedure takes this cap rather than the procedural one, which is why text_type classification (see metrics.md) decides which of the two rules applies rather than document location.

Source: ASD-STE100
  ASD-STE100 rule 4.3 (Issue 9)
  The specification states the rule as a direction rather than a threshold, so the four-item trigger is our operational choice: three coordinated items still read cleanly inline, and the count is what a checker can measure. The formatting sub-requirements of this rule are separate mechanizable rules below.

Source: ASD-STE100
  ASD-STE100 rule 1.14 (Issue 9)
  Generated from the locale table rather than written as a rule, because the correct spelling depends on the project and a rule's substitution map has only one direction. Source: Retired Vale style — docs-discipline/StatusLanguage.yml
  E1 in the retired slop-lint.py. The negative lookahead on `currently` exempts runtime-state description (currently running/active/...), which is legitimate present tense, not doc status. Relaxed is advisory rather than excluded because a false status claim is a factual defect, not a register preference. .vale.ini turns it off for the package's own normative source files, which quote the ban list they enforce. Go->Python: the lookahead `(?!...)` is RE2-safe and ports unchanged.
